title: Central TermAl host crashed: "memory allocation of 2719744 bytes failed" (0xc0000409) at 17:08Z during the Engram baa6 Windows FULL
outcome: The Central host does not die when system commit runs low: test-run placement keeps enough commit headroom for the host, and the host degrades or refuses work rather than aborting on a failed allocation. The cause of the 17:08Z commit exhaustion is identified from measurements.
acceptance: The 2026-11-14 17:08:27Z crash is explained from evidence (commit charge and the largest consumers at that time: the Engram baa6 Windows FULL started 17:05Z, rustc/test processes, Node, Chrome, the host itself), not from the exit code alone.
Central placement rules (capacity memory central-cargo-memory-budget) cover FULLs on Central with a commit-based floor that would have prevented this, recorded and applied by the integration owner.
If the host's own abort on allocation failure is avoidable (for example a bounded allocation on a hot path), that is filed or fixed separately with a behavioural test.
